newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. data pushes German shares to end bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data pushes German shares to end bourse lower.

text.p: German equities ended bourse trade sharply lower on Friday as Wall Street's overnight drop and the continued weakness of the dollar depressed trading sentiment on the German stock exchange.

The Dow Jones index of U.S. blue-chips closed over one percent lower on Thursday, and the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips took its cue from Wall Street to end floor trade down 18.45 points at 2,543.83 points.
As anticipated, support for the DAX held at 2,540 points.
With little corporate news due on Friday, and a holiday in the U.S. on Monday next, dealers were pessimistic about any new direction for the market until Tuesday.
U.S. GDP data for the second quarter showed a 4.8 percent increase, prompting fears of the first U.S. interest rate increase since February 1995.

One trader said that Daimler Benz AG, which reported a massive improvement in first half profitability on Thursday, would trade lower over the day as there were no further expectations to drive the share higher.
Shares in Daimler ended floor trade 75 pfennigs lower at 80.55 marks.
Engineering group Mannesmann AG ended bourse up 2.50 marks at 534 marks, after unconfirmed market rumours that the share had been upgraded by analysts.
